MP35N and ODS MP35N blocks of size of 20×20×10 mm3 were fabricated by the LPBF process using pre-alloyed MP35N powders and acoustically-mixed powders (consisting of MP35N and 1wt.% Y2O3).

For the LPBF process, an FS271 machine equipped with a Nd: YAG fiber laser and protective Ar gas environment was used. The utilized laser energy density for printing the blocks were within the range of 80-100 J mm–3. Besides, the scan strategy of 67° scan rotation was used for both alloys to reduce the microstructural anisotropy between each layer.

Firstly, the high friction stress of the ODS MP35N MPEA stems from the higher solid solution strengthening of the MP35N matrix alloy, due to the presence of 6.2 at.% large-sized refractory Mo contents, which results in larger lattice distortion (i.e. mean square atomic displacement) than CoCrNi-based MPEAs (including Al0.5CoCrFeNi) [19].

Secondly, the high grain boundary strengthening of the ODS MP35N MPEA originates from the relatively low SFE of the matrix alloy (i.e. of ∼ 9mJ/m2 [21]) than CoCrNi and Al0.5CoCrFeNi as mentioned before. The low SFE promotes perfect dislocations dissociation (i.e. suppresses partial dislocations recombination) and hence reduces the extent of dislocation cross slip. Consequently, the ability of dislocations transferring across grain boundary via cross slip is reduced [36], which gives rise to a high extent of dislocation pile-up upon grain boundaries and leads to high grain boundary strengthening ability of the investigated ODS MP35N MPEA.
Thirdly, the high dislocation strengthening comes from the solidification dislocation cell structure, which is inherent to alloys fabricated by LPBF due to the rapid heating and cooling cycles [32].
